properties.name: WHAT WORKED (2026-10-02, 0.77.0, through the --call door): a refused import_graph writes nothing and lists every bad item at once, and create_edges with check_only validates a whole batch and writes nothing. Both ride the core's atomic batch, the property the typed constructors lack. Do not regress it
properties.statement:
From art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02, two "Measured" rows:
- "import_graph of a hand-built document (about 110 nodes, 140 edges) — written in one call, nothing skipped; a refused import writes nothing";
- "create_edges with check_only: true — validates the batch and writes nothing".

RE-MEASURED by triage agent C on reflow2-mcp 0.77.0, scratch stores. Log: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-C/measure.log.
(1) main's committed export, 6,309 nodes and 41,546 edges, imported in one call, exit 0, in 4.4 s.
(2) A document holding two edges the schema refuses (REALIZES Artifact→Decision, VERIFIES Verification→Decision) was refused by import_graph and by CLI --import. Both were listed with their index, the REALIZES one naming the edge that fits (DOCUMENTS), and a node from the same document was absent afterwards (get_node null). One blemish: the CLI --import left an empty store directory behind.
(3) create_edges check_only with one valid and one invalid edge: applied false, would_apply false, checked 2, and the one failure named with its index.

WHY IT MATTERS: both go through the store's atomic batch (bulk.rs atomic(), begin_batch/commit_batch/discard_batch), per dec:bulk-is-all-or-nothing-with-per-item-findings. The typed single-node constructors do not, and a refusal there leaves the node behind (fact:root-cause-a-typed-constructor-writes-the-node-before-its-later-checks-and-a-refusal-leaves-it-2026-10-02). A fix for that should reuse this path, not weaken it.
